name: Gwangju AI Industry Convergence Cluster National AI Data Center
developer: Gwangju Metropolitan City / Korea AI Convergence Industry Cluster project; operated by NHN (NHN Cloud) under a national AI data center service
notes: The Gwangju AI-specialized data center, core facility of the Gwangju AI industry convergence cluster in the Advanced 3 District (Cheomdan 3), Buk-gu Oryong-dong near GIST, broke ground 2021-11-22; NHN was selected as cloud infrastructure builder/operator (2021) with 88.5 PF HPC planned from end-2022. The cluster comprises three buildings totalling about 47,256 sqm; national AI data center services began recruiting users from April 2026. No public MW figure found.

name: Hyundai AutoEver Gwangju Data Center
notes: Hyundai AutoEver's official workplace page lists its Gwangju data center at 75 Jingok Industrial Complex Central-ro (Jingok Industrial Complex), Gwangsan-gu, Gwangju. The Hyundai Motor Group invested about KRW 50 billion; local reporting describes a roughly 2,070 pyeong, two-storey facility on a 6,000 pyeong site with full operation targeted from January 2017. Enterprise/corporate data center; no public MW figure found.

name: National Information Resources Service (NIRS) Gwangju Center
developer: National Information Resources Service / Ministry of the Interior and Safety (government)
notes: NIRS Gwangju Center is a government consolidated/backup data center located at 34 Songam-ro 143beon-gil, Songam-dong, Seo-gu, Gwangju (address confirmed by parking/EV-charging listing and Wikipedia; operational notices published via gov.kr and NIRS official site). No public MW capacity published.

name: Kakao Data Center Ansan
notes: Kakao's first self-built hyperscale data center, located inside Hanyang University's ERICA campus in Ansan-si (Sangnok-gu); construction began 2021 and operations started around Q1 2024. Facility is about 47,378 sqm with 4,000 racks designed to host 120,000 servers; Kakao's CEO visited in December 2024 to review operations. No public MW figure found in sources reviewed.

name: NH Financial Group Anseong Data Center
notes: inews24 reports the Anseong Fire Department conducted fire-safety field guidance at the NH Financial Group Anseong data center in Gongdo-eup (공도읍), Anseong-si, following the NIRS data center fire, confirming an operating financial-group data center in the county. No public MW figure or opening date found in sources reviewed.

name: Hanwha Solution Anseong Data Center
developer: Hanwha Solution (project SPC, Muwa Jade) with Hanwha E&C construction division as builder
notes: Newspim (2026-05-20) reports Hanwha's construction division is building the Hanwha Solution Anseong data center, an around KRW 80-81.5 billion construction project (Hanwha E&C listed the Anseong data center among its data center works at 81.5 billion won construction cost); Hanwha e-Pyeonhanse world history pages reference an 'Anseong data center' special purpose company (Muwa Jade). In construction as of mid-2026; no public MW figure found.

name: LG U+ Pyeongchon 2 Center (Anyang IDC)
notes: LG U+ completed its new hyperscale IDC 'Pyeongchon 2 Center' in Gwanak-dong, Dongan-gu, Anyang-si in October 2023: nine above-ground and three underground floors, about 44,500 sqm, sized to hold over 200,000 servers. LG U+'s official IDC page lists the Anyang center (Pyeongchon cluster, which also hosts the earlier Pyeongchon 1 IDC). No public MW figure found.

name: Evrisho / STT GDC Anyang IDC (Hogye-dong)
developer: Evrisho, joint venture of Hyosung Heavy Industries and STT GDC
notes: Hankook Ilbo (2023-02-13) reports the Evrisho JV (Hyosung Heavy Industries and Singapore's STT GDC) planned an IDC on a 12,627 sqm site in Hogye-dong, Anyang-si with a 62 m tall, two-basement/eight-above-ground-floor building, but faced intense resident opposition (banners, petitions and inspections requests) as of February 2023; Anyang city said procedures were lawful. Project status beyond planning could not be confirmed in later public sources; treated as planned with opposition risk.
